title: Athaliah
lead: Daughter (or granddaughter) of Omri's house, wife of King Jehoram of Judah and mother of Ahaziah, who seized Judah's throne after her son's death and ruled for six years (about 841–835 BC), the only woman to rule Israel or Judah in her own right in the biblical period (before the Hasmonean queen Salome Alexandra), until the priest Jehoiada crowned the boy Joash.

sections.b: Athaliah is called the daughter of Ahab (2 Kings 8:18) and the "daughter" of Omri, which may mean granddaughter (2 Kings 8:26). Her marriage to Jehoram of Judah sealed the alliance between Omri's house and David's. When Jehu killed her son Ahaziah, she destroyed the royal line and reigned, but one baby, Joash, was hidden in the temple (2 Kings 11:1–3; 2 Chronicles 22:10–12). Kings gives her no regnal formula, as if her reign did not count. Chronicles blames her and her sons for plundering the temple for Baal (2 Chronicles 24:7).
